operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: BDBV Outbreak Surpasses 1,200 Cases — Uganda Closes DRC Border as Response Reaches Critical Juncture
heroSubtitle: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak accelerated sharply through May 27–28, with total suspected and confirmed cases surpassing 1,205 (up from 906 on May 26) and confirmed deaths rising to 18 as the Mongbwalu crisis generated cascading secondary transmission. Uganda announced a 4-week closure of all DRC border crossings on May 28 — the first such closure by any country and a direct departure from WHO IHR guidance — as 7 lab-confirmed cases were traced to Kampala. The U.S. finalized an additional $80 million bilateral assistance package, bringing total U.S. commitment to ~$135 million. Oxford University and the Serum Institute of India confirmed their ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine candidate could enter Phase 1 human trials within 2–3 months, accelerating the prior 6–9 month estimate. Of the 25 suspected BDBV patients who escaped Mongbwalu ETU attacks between May 23–26, none had been located as of May 28; DRC contact tracing coverage fell below 45% against the 80% containment threshold.
footerNote: Data sourced from WHO Situation Reports, DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE), Uganda Ministry of Health, CDC Emergency Operations, ECDC, MSF field reports, U.S. State Department, Oxford University Jenner Institute, and institutional analyses. Case counts and CFR figures are rapidly evolving.
